blockers.quote: by day forty-eight it is bigger than everything the whole world makes in a year (about $128 trillion, IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026)
blockers.why: The packaging (premise) asserts as an established fact that global yearly output is 'about $128 trillion' cited to the October 2026 IMF World Economic Outlook, but this figure has no claim row in claims.md and needs a source (standard nominal Gross World Product projections are approximately $110-$121 trillion). Under G1 rules, an unsourced fact stated as true in packaging is a blocker.
blockers.fix: by day forty-eight it is bigger than everything the whole world makes in a year (world yearly output needs a source), and by day fifty-eight it overflows the number box most computers count in.

blockers.quote: 6:45, "day fifty-eight is square sixty-four" (what happens on sixty-four?).
blockers.why: Mathematically false. Square 64 of a chessboard holds 2^63 grains (9,223,372,036,854,775,808). Starting from $1 (100 cents) on day one, day fifty-eight holds 100 * 2^57 = 14,411,518,807,585,587,200 cents (~1.56 * 2^63 cents). Square 64 of cents was crossed during day fifty-seven. While line 43 was corrected in round 5 to remove the chessboard comparison, line 61 still quotes 'day fifty-eight is square sixty-four' as an open loop.
blockers.fix: 6:45, "day fifty-eight overflows the sixty-fourth bit" (what happens on sixty-four bits?).

blockers.quote: You put down a deposit on a flat with a view, because you think day thirty-one might just cover it.
blockers.why: Violates the wrong belief rule (rules/story.md #7: the misconception must be described fairly as people actually hold it, not as a straw man). Line 36 explicitly establishes that on day twenty-five the balance is already $16.8 million (and on day twenty with $524,288 you could already buy a flat). Presenting a person who already holds $16.8 million as believing that six more doublings to day thirty-one ($1.07 billion) 'might just cover' a deposit on a flat is an implausible straw man rather than genuine exponential growth bias.
blockers.fix: Move the flat deposit to an earlier beat when the balance is small (e.g. day fifteen at $16,384 or day twenty at $524,288), or reframe the day thirty-one expectation to an asset scale that plausibly tests human intuition (e.g. thinking day thirty-one might cover buying a superyacht or an entire block).
